definitions.explanation: The tendency to put on airs or make things look fancier than they are. Most commonly used in the negative form (飾り気のない) to praise someone or something as unpretentious.

examples.japanese: {飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない{人|ひと}だ。
{飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない{言葉|ことば}で{気持|きも}ちを{伝|つた}えた。
examples.english: I expressed my feelings in plain, unadorned words.

examples.japanese: あの{店|みせ}は{飾|かざ}り{気|け}がなくて{落|お}ち{着|つ}いた{雰囲気|ふんいき}がある。
examples.english: That shop has an unpretentious, relaxed atmosphere.

notes:
USAGE:
{飾|かざ}り{気|け} is overwhelmingly used in the negative pattern {飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない or {飾|かざ}り{気|け}がない, meaning "unpretentious" or "unaffected." This is a compliment, praising natural simplicity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない{人|ひと} (an unpretentious person)
- {飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない{言葉|ことば} (plain, honest words)
- {飾|かざ}り{気|け}のない{笑顔|えがお} (a natural smile)
- {飾|かざ}り{気|け}がない (to be unpretentious)
